summary: The proof is complete and correct. Part 1 establishes termination via the well-founded lexicographic measure (K, Ω) where K = count of integers >1 and Ω = total prime factors with multiplicity, and proves K=1 at termination by showing K never drops below 1. Part 2 identifies the invariant G_p = gcd of p-adic valuations (which equals the gcd of initial exponents for each prime), and uses the Part 1 termination result (exactly one M>1, rest are 1) to conclude v_p(M) = G_p. The final integer M = ∏ p^{G_p} is uniquely determined by the initial multiset. All load-bearing implications are valid; the redundant per-prime sum-decrease argument in 'Behaviour of p-adic valuations' does not create a logical gap because the core deduction uses the already-proved global termination. No invalid inferences found; no fixes required.
